tech.tagline: AI & software for health and business

services.title: AI / ML model development
services.tagline: Classification, prediction and imaging models for biomedical datasets.
services.problem: Clinics, labs and health startups sit on data they cannot turn into decisions: images nobody has time to screen, measurements nobody has modelled. Generic ML tooling ignores how biological data is really collected, noisy, small and biased, so models look great in a demo and fail on the next batch.

steps.name: SCOPE
steps.text: Pin down the decision the model must support, the data you hold and what "good enough" means.

steps.name: AUDIT DATA
steps.text: Check quality, leakage, class balance and labelling before any model is trained.

steps.name: BASELINE
steps.text: Start with simple, explainable models so every later gain is measured against something honest.

steps.name: TRAIN & VALIDATE
steps.text: Cross-validated training with a held-out test set that the model never sees until the end.

steps.name: EXPLAIN
steps.text: Error analysis and plain-language reporting: where it works, where it does not, and why.

steps.name: HAND OVER
steps.text: Reproducible notebook, evaluation report and a small API so your team can run it without me.

deliverables: Small inference API and usage notes

timeline.style: Weekly check-ins, shared notebook from day one

faq.q: Do I need a lot of data?
faq.a: Not always. Biomedical datasets are often small, so I choose methods that suit that, and I will tell you early if the data is not enough to support the question.
Yes. Every project includes a plain-language report, not just numbers, covering what the model can and cannot be trusted for.

services.title: Bioinformatics & genomics analysis
services.tagline: Sequence and expression data analysis, visualisation and clear summaries.
services.problem: Sequencing and expression data arrive as huge tables that are hard to read and easy to misinterpret. Teams without a dedicated bioinformatician either wait weeks for results or draw conclusions the data does not support.

steps.name: QUESTION
steps.text: Turn the biological question into a testable analysis plan.

steps.name: QC
steps.text: Quality control and normalisation so differences you see are biology, not artefacts.

steps.name: ANALYSE
steps.text: Differential expression, variant or sequence analysis suited to the question.

steps.name: INTERPRET
steps.text: Pathway and annotation context, with the statistics stated honestly.

steps.name: VISUALISE
steps.text: Publication-style figures plus interactive views you can explore.

steps.name: REPORT
steps.text: A written summary, the code and the figures, so the work can be repeated and checked.

deliverables: Figures ready for slides or papers

timeline.style: Short written updates at each stage

faq.a: [EDIT: list exactly what you are comfortable with, e.g. RNA-seq counts, protein structures, sequence alignments.]

faq.q: Can you help me write it up?
faq.a: Yes. Methods and results text, and figure captions, are part of the deliverables.
Methods and multiple-testing handling are stated in the report, so a reviewer can follow every step.
